contract: Every public-facing surface that renders a booking or profile page for a member of an organisation must resolve that page's visual identity — brandColor, darkBrandColor and the light/dark `theme` preference — from the organisation the member belongs to whenever the member is viewed in an org context, exactly as team-owned pages already resolve theirs from the owning Team row. Any query that loads the data for such a page must therefore select the organisation's branding columns, any type carrying that data must be able to express them, and any code that assembles the `profile` object handed to the Booker/UserPage must apply the org value as the styling basis (with the personal value only as a fallback), so that a single organisation renders identically regardless of whether a visitor arrives via a team link or a member's personal link.

defect_location.summary: The styling basis for public pages is chosen in `packages/features/eventtypes/lib/getPublicEvent.ts:585-613`: `getProfileFromEvent` sets `const styleProfile = team || event.parent?.team || nonTeamProfile` (line 591) and then emits `brandColor: styleProfile.brandColor`, `darkBrandColor: styleProfile.darkBrandColor`, `theme: styleProfile.theme` (lines 606-608). For a team event the basis is the Team row, whose branding columns ARE selected (packages/features/eventtypes/lib/getPublicEvent.ts:91-112, and the managed-parent team at :155-165), so team pages honour the organisation's appearance. For a personal event the basis is the user, and the user's own `organization` relation is selected with only `id, name, slug, bannerUrl` (packages/features/eventtypes/lib/getPublicEvent.ts:41-48) — the org's `brandColor`/`darkBrandColor`/`theme` are never loaded and never consulted, so the page falls back to the member's personal colours. The same omission repeats on the dynamic-group path, which hard-codes `brandColor: users[0].brandColor, darkBrandColor: users[0].darkBrandColor, theme: null` (packages/features/eventtypes/lib/getPublicEvent.ts:338-353) even after it has fetched org details at :309-319. The public profile page repeats it independently: `apps/web/server/lib/[user]/getServerSideProps.ts:133-145` builds `profile` as `theme: user.theme, brandColor: user.brandColor ?? DEFAULT_LIGHT_BRAND_COLOR, darkBrandColor: user.darkBrandColor ?? DEFAULT_DARK_BRAND_COLOR` with no org consultation, and `apps/web/modules/users/views/users-public-view.tsx:29` applies only `useTheme(profile.theme)`. The org object that would supply the missing values cannot carry them today: `packages/features/profile/repositories/ProfileRepository.ts:44-53` selects `id, slug, name, metadata, logoUrl, bannerUrl, isPlatform, hideBranding` and nothing else, and the type in `packages/types/UserProfile.d.ts:3-5` is `Pick<Team, "name" | "id" | "slug" | "calVideoLogo", "bannerUrl">`; the user query behind the personal page (`packages/features/users/repositories/UserRepository.ts:169-179` using `userSelect` at :82-122) likewise selects only the user's own `theme`/`brandColor`/`darkBrandColor` (:96, :107-108). Confirming that the org row does hold these values and is written only on itself: `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/update.handler.ts:204-218` persists `brandColor`, `darkBrandColor` and `theme` on the organisation Team row alone, with no propagation to members. Consumers of the produced profile — `packages/platform/atoms/booker/BookerWebWrapper.tsx:204-206`, `apps/web/app/(booking-page-wrapper)/team/[slug]/[type]/queries.ts:88`, `apps/web/server/lib/[user]/[type]/getServerSideProps.ts:155,247` and `apps/web/lib/d/[link]/[slug]/getServerSideProps.tsx:117` — pass the values straight through, so the divergence originates in the resolvers and selects named above.
